content.text:
I changed `resolveGlobBase` in `packages/isomorphic/urlMatch.ts` so it only replaces parts of the pattern that contain glob special characters (`*`, `?`, `{`, `}`, backslash) with placeholders. Literal parts now go through `new URL` resolution as they did in 1.50. I haven't built or run anything, so none of this is tested.

- **Default ports:** a pattern like `http://localhost:80/**` should now resolve to `http://localhost/**`, so it matches the request URL.
- **Other normalizations:** a literal space should come out as `%20`, and `münchen.de` should come out as its punycode form.
- **Question marks:** the `?` and everything after it in a part is still replaced with a placeholder. A literal prefix before the `?` is now left to URL resolution, which is what I expect keeps the earlier question-mark fix working.

One thing I left alone: a literal `#` in a pattern part is no longer replaced, so URL parsing will treat it as a fragment start, as it did before 1.51. I didn't add `#` to the special characters because the issue didn't list it.

`resolveGlobBase` now replaces a pattern part with a placeholder only if it contains `*`, `?`, `{`, `}` or a backslash. Literal parts go through `new URL` as they did in 1.50. That should bring back default-port dropping (`http://localhost:80/**`), `%20` encoding and punycode hosts. The part from a `?` onward is still always replaced, so the earlier question-mark fix should keep working.

A literal `#` in a pattern part is no longer replaced, so URL parsing will treat it as a fragment start, as it did before 1.51. I left `#` out of the special characters because the issue didn't list it.
